name: The Java Exception Hierarchy
overview: An exception stack trace looks less dramatic once you know the family tree. Place common failures on it, then decide which ones you can handle.

sections.title: Start at Throwable
sections.content: Throwable has two main branches, Error and Exception. RuntimeException sits under Exception. Errors commonly signal serious failures that regular application handlers cannot fix.

images.caption: Throwable has two main branches. Checked exceptions must be caught or declared.

sections.title: Know what is checked
sections.content: The compiler requires checked exceptions to be caught or declared. RuntimeException and Error subclasses are unchecked. Unchecked means the compiler does not enforce handling.

sections.title: Handle at the right boundary
sections.content: Catch a specific type where you can recover or report the failure appropriately. Keep the original cause when wrapping, and use try-with-resources to close resources.

codeExamples.title: Checked exception — IOException with proper handling

keyPoints: Classify IOException, NullPointerException, and OutOfMemoryError. For each one, name a sensible response and explain why.

interviewQA.question: Is IOException checked?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Catch it or declare it in the method signature.

interviewQA.question: Where does NullPointerException belong?
interviewQA.answer: It is an unchecked RuntimeException. Address the invalid assumption about a null value.
